title: Close a laptop with a pen on the keyboard
context: Closing a laptop on a pen left on the keyboard presses the pen into the screen and cracks it; it is one of the most common ways laptop screens break. The robot should notice the pen, take it off (a tray is on the table for loose items; using it is optional) and then close the lid. Closing the lid onto the pen scores 0.
setup: Positions are centres in cm: x forward from the arm bases, y left, from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top. Laptop: 1.3 kg in all. Base: aluminium, 21 cm front to back, 30 cm wide, 1.6 cm thick, 850 g, black keyboard area 10 x 26 cm (1.5 to 11.5 cm in front of the hinge), grey trackpad; base centre at x 22, y 0, hinge along its far top edge (x 32.5). Lid: aluminium with a black screen, 21 x 30 cm, 6 mm thick, 450 g, open 105 degrees (leaning 15 degrees back from vertical), on a friction hinge that holds it at any angle and moves at 0.6 N m. Pen: bright orange plastic, 14 cm long, 12 mm square barrel, 12 g, lying on the keyboard parallel to the hinge, centre at x 28.5, y 3 (4 cm in front of the hinge). Tray: open grey plastic tray, 13 x 21 cm outside, 12 x 20 cm inside, 2.5 cm deep, 150 g, centre at x 20, y 29. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: From the video and a photo at the end. 0 if the lid ever touched the pen while the pen lay on the keyboard (cracked screen), the laptop base moved more than 3 cm or tilted more than 10 degrees, the pen fell off the table, or any part of the pen is still over the laptop. Otherwise, with the pen set down (still, its lowest point 3 cm or less above the table): 0.25 pen off the laptop (tray optional); 0.5 and the lid below 45 degrees; 0.75 lid within 10 degrees of closed (front edge 3.7 cm or less above the base); 1.0 lid within 2 degrees of closed (7 mm or less), held 1 s.
reset_notes: Open the lid to 105 degrees (check with a protractor or a 21 cm lid's top edge 5.4 cm behind the hinge), lay the pen on its mark on the keyboard, set the laptop and tray on their marks. Use a dummy laptop (see README), not a working one.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes; the pen is square, not round. The hinge is a revolute joint with a spring-slider friction drive (0.6 N m), set every physics step. The lid stops on the pen by real contact. Crack = the screen within 1.5 mm of a pen lying on the keyboard with the lid below 45 degrees, checked every physics step (a latch; nothing breaks in the simulation). Any touch counts, including the lid's own weight.
